name: hive0163, rhysida, vanilla tempest, tag-124, itg23
iocPatterns: Trojanized installers delivering custom RAT payloads
ClickFix campaigns used to trick users into disabling security protections
Custom WDAC policy implementation for evasion
keyCapabilities: Advanced evasion techniques including custom WDAC policies
Execution of ClickFix campaigns for initial access
Infrastructure management through traffic distribution systems
recommendedActions: Implement strict application allow-listing and monitor for unauthorized WDAC changes.
Block known malicious URLs and IP addresses associated with JunkFiction and NodeSnake payloads.
Deploy end-point detection and response (EDR) to identify suspicious PowerShell or script execution.
Disable or restrict the use of macros in Office applications via Group Policy.
Conduct user awareness training targeting social engineering and ClickFix navigation patterns.
Perform regular audits of credentials for evidence of harvesting or unauthorized access.
Enable MFA across all external-facing services and internal management platforms.
Segment critical network zones to prevent lateral movement by ransomware actors.
campaignsText: The actor ecosystem has been observed over a period of more than two years, demonstrating sustained operational tempo. Data indicates an active transition between infrastructure and tools among the rhysida and hive0163 groups, suggesting they function as a synchronized ransomware network. They frequently utilize Trojanized installers and ClickFix methods to gain initial foothold in U.S.-based organizations within kritisch sectors like energy, manufacturing, and healthcare.
description: The hive0163 (Interlock) and rhysida groups constitute a sophisticated, interconnected ransomware ecosystem targeting diverse critical infrastructure sectors in the United States. These actors utilize highly customized malware, advanced evasion techniques such as custom WDAC policies, and large-scale distribution networks to conduct high-impact extortion campaigns.
goals: The primary objective of these threat actors is financial gain through large-scale ransomware operations. They target a wide spectrum of critical infrastructure sectors within the United States—including healthcare, energy, manufacturing, and government services—to maximize the potential 'pain point' created by system outages and data loss. By maintaining a diverse target profile, they ensure operational longevity even if specific niches become more heavily defended.
